conventions.convention: C_n means Cl_(0,n): vector multiplication squares to minus the squared Euclidean norm. Module parity, algebra word parity, and volume chirality are distinct.
KO and KSp use finite-rank bundles with locally constant finite-valued rank, permitting different ranks on finitely many clopen strata. Quaternionic bundles are right modules.
Relative KO uses the based quotient X/A; when A is empty use X_+. Negative degrees are defined by suspension, and the rank-zero Thom space is X_+.
M_n retains graded modules; A_n is coker(M_(n+1)→M_n). At n=0, M_0 has separate even and odd generators, and the quotient coordinate is even dimension minus odd dimension.
For positive rank divisible by four, the volume Thom source is the ungraded module group. North-section subtraction gives Ψ=[H(Λ)]−π*[Λ+], while the source-minus-target volume symbol is Φ=−Ψ.

Spin and Spin-c structures are supplied lifts, not asserted to exist. Spin uses the negative-definite norm-one even subgroup, including Spin(0)={±1}; the complex Spin-c spinor representation has central weight one.
The trace metric is −tr(AB)/p. Nonunitary index estimates are non-strict and require additional slack; unitary stages retain determinant winding rather than identifying all path components.

Mass differences retain a specified identification of the fixed Clifford representations. The comparison uses negative-eigenspace rank, uniformly negating the auxiliary positive-rank clutching convention.
The normalized simultaneous AZ algebra imposes TC=CT. Real indices are AI through CI at q=0 through 7, and d fixed negative-square Dirac generators shift the index to q−d.

load_bearing.statement: Assume AC. Let X be finite CW and V oriented Euclidean of positive rank 4m. Every real bundle on S(R⊕V) becomes π*E_0⊕H(Λ) after addition of finitely many trivial real bundles and copies of H(C(V)); the prescribed relative splitting and lower-disk gauge extend under the stated rank, winding and relative-cell-dimension inequalities.

Assume AC. For finite CW X and oriented Euclidean V of positive rank 4m, if π*E_0⊕H(Λ) and π*E_1⊕H(M) become isomorphic after the same trivial and regular Hopf additions, then E_0,E_1 are ordinarily stably isomorphic and Λ,M become isomorphic after equal regular module additions.

Assume AC. For finite CW X and oriented Euclidean V of positive rank 4m, Ψ_V:K_C(V)(X)→reduced KO^0(Th(V)), [Λ]↦[H(Λ)]−π*[Λ+], is an isomorphism. The volume-positive source-minus-target symbol is Φ_V=−Ψ_V.
Assume AC. For k=4m−1, d≥1 and a positive orthogonal C_k representation on R^p, the affine Hopf inclusion in stable winding η is d-connected for finite CW pairs when p≥p_0(d,k) and s_k d≤η≤p/4.

Assume AC. Relative KO on finite CW pairs is the group of bundle triples modulo isomorphism, additivity, homotopy and elementary extensions; homotopic pair maps induce equal maps. Finite trivial complements and common trivial stabilization exist, also over H. These conclusions extend to compact Hausdorff pairs with closed subspace.

Assume AC. Multiplication by the same volume-positive rank-eight real spinor symbol β is a natural isomorphism KO^j(X,A)→KO^(j−8)(X,A) for every finite CW pair and every integer j, with positive degrees defined by periodic continuation.

Assume AC. The actual graded negative-square Clifford symbol satisfies ker(s_n)=im(r_n) and induces α_n:A_n≅KO^(−n)(pt). These maps are multiplicative, and the chosen degree-eight generator maps to the same β used for real Bott periodicity.

Assume AC. The stated stable difference group D_q of positive Clifford mass extensions, retaining its fixed-representation identification, has a natural additive isomorphism Ψ_q:D_q→KO^(−q)(pt). At q=0 it is negative-eigenspace rank difference, and explicit eightfold stabilization corresponds to product with β.

concerns.concern: The Statement begins “For a given Spin bundle V→X of positive rank 8m” and gives the rank-8m+4 branch without specifying a finite CW base. Proof 1.1 composes thm-real-clifford-thom-isomorphism and lem-real-and-quaternionic-spinor-module-morita-evaluation, both explicitly restricted to finite CW X. The supplied argument therefore needs that base hypothesis stated here; the local KO definition only defines the bundle groups on compact Hausdorff spaces and does not supply the missing finite-CW scope.

seams_checked.note: The prerequisite page and actual classification, even-subalgebra, PBW and graded-tensor interfaces agree with the consumer's translation C_n=Cl_(0,n). The consumer uses nondegenerate Euclidean forms, preserves Koszul signs, and separates graded module groups from ungraded Morita groups. The supplier page describes KO/ABS as downstream rather than assuming their conclusions.

The actual group definition, algebraic image/kernel theorem and topological double-cover theorem support the definite negative-square Spin lifts used here, including the explicit Spin(0)={±1} convention. The consumer assumes given lifts and does not import an existence criterion or extend definite compactness to mixed signature. The supplier page keeps its representation and covering claims distinct from downstream KO orientations.
